transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is that I just feel… wound up, pretty much all the time. Like my body is constantly bracing for something bad to happen, even when there’s no obvious reason. I can be sitting at my desk at work, doing computer support stuff, and I’m technically just answering tickets or trying to focus, but my shoulders are tight and I feel like I’m on alert.

And it’s not only at work. Even when I’m doing something I normally enjoy, like dance night, I still feel this tension in me, like I can’t fully relax into it. It’s like part of me is waiting for the next problem, the next bad thing, and I’m tired of feeling like that.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, like work, relationships, or other everyday issues, even when there isn’t a clear reason to be concerned?

Yes… definitely. It’s like my worry doesn’t stay in one place anymore. At first I think I was more focused on the condo and practical stuff around that, but now it kind of jumps around all day.

Like I’ll be wondering if my cousin is upset with me because of something I said, and I’ll replay the conversation in my head and try to figure out if her tone seemed different. Then I’ll be at work and suddenly it’s about whether I’m going to make some dumb mistake on a support call, or miss something obvious, or sound incompetent. And then later it turns into bigger life stuff, like how I’m ever going to save enough money, or move forward, or feel like I’m not falling behind everyone else.

It’s not always that there’s a clear problem happening right then. Sometimes there’s nothing specific, and my mind just… finds something to attach to. And once it does, it feels hard to let it go.
Do you often experience physical symptoms like restlessness, fatigue, or muscle tension when you’re feeling anxious?

Yes, especially the tension and that restless, wound-up feeling. It’s kind of the main reason I came in, honestly. I feel like my body is bracing for something bad to happen, even when there isn’t anything happening.

Like I’ll just be sitting at my desk at work, answering tickets or staring at a screen, and my shoulders are already up near my ears, or I realize I’m holding myself really rigid. And it’s not even always because something stressful just happened. It’s more like my body is already preparing for the next thing to go wrong.

Even when I’m supposed to be relaxing, like at dance night, I’ll notice I’m still tense inside. I want to enjoy it and just be there, but part of me feels on alert, like I can’t fully let go. It’s exhausting in a way, because I don’t feel like I get many moments where my body actually believes I’m safe or settled.
Do you ever feel this anxious or tense even when you’re completely alone and there’s no immediate situation, person, or task causing stress?

Yes. Honestly, that’s part of what feels so frustrating about it, because it doesn’t always need a trigger. I can be completely by myself, with nothing actively happening, and I’ll still feel like my body is waiting for something bad to happen.

Like I’ll just be sitting at my desk, or at home, or even trying to do something that should be enjoyable, and there’s this wound-up feeling in me. My shoulders get tight, and I feel like I’m bracing, almost like I’m preparing for the next problem before I even know what it is.

And with dance night, too — even though I want to relax and enjoy it, I’ll notice I’m still tense inside. It’s not necessarily that someone said anything or that there’s some immediate task I’m stressed about. It’s more like my body hasn’t gotten the message that everything is okay. It just stays on alert.
How often do these anxious feelings and the physical tension happen—like, are they present most days, or do they come and go more sporadically?

It’s most days. I wish it were more like it came and went in a clear way, but it feels pretty constant lately.

I mean, it may get louder or quieter depending on what I’m doing, but the baseline is usually there — like I’m wound up, or my body is bracing for the next bad thing. Even if I’m just sitting at my desk, not in the middle of anything dramatic, I’ll notice I’m tight and tense, like I’m already preparing for something to go wrong.

And then even during things I actually want to enjoy, like dance night, it doesn’t fully switch off. I might be trying to have fun, but there’s still this tension underneath it, like I can’t completely relax. So… yeah, I’d say it’s there most days, not just once in a while.
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you know it might not make sense or there's nothing specific to worry about?

Yes. That’s actually one of the parts that bothers me the most, because I can sometimes see that the worry isn’t really helping, but I still can’t just… shut it off.

Like at work, I’ll tell myself, “Okay, I already checked the spreadsheet,” or “I already sent that email, it’s done,” but then my brain keeps circling back to it anyway. I’ll start wondering, what if I missed something, what if I sent it to the wrong person, what if there was an attachment issue, what if someone reads it the wrong way. And then it’s like one “what if” turns into five more before I can pull myself back.

Even when there isn’t one clear thing to worry about, my mind kind of searches for something. I can know logically that I did the task, or checked it, or handled it, but the thoughts keep looping like they don’t believe me. It’s exhausting because I’ll try to reassure myself, but it only works for a little bit, if at all.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel an intense wave of fear or discomfort that comes on very quickly, like your heart starts racing, you feel short of breath, or like something terrible is going to happen right then and there?

I’m not really sure I’d describe it that way. I mean, I definitely get anxious and tense, and sometimes it can feel really uncomfortable, but I don’t know that I’ve had those sudden, out-of-nowhere waves where it’s like everything spikes all at once and I feel like something terrible is happening right that second.

For me it feels more like this ongoing buildup or background tension, if that makes sense. Like I can be worrying and feeling keyed up for a long time, and it might get worse depending on what I’m thinking about, but it doesn’t usually feel like a distinct episode that suddenly comes on super fast and then passes. At least, I haven’t really noticed it in that clear way.

I guess I do sometimes feel very uncomfortable in my body when I’m anxious, but I’m not sure about the heart racing or shortness of breath part specifically. If it happens, I don’t think I’ve been labeling it as a separate episode. It’s more like… I’m just anxious and wound up, not like a sudden attack of fear.
Has this constant worry and tension made it harder for you to function in your daily life, like at work, in social situations, or with personal relationships?

Yes, it has. I think that’s actually where it started feeling less like “I’m just stressed” and more like… okay, this is getting in the way of my life.

At work, I’m a computer support specialist, so there are always tickets coming in, and I used to be pretty good at moving through them. Not perfectly, but I could prioritize and get things done. Lately I’ve been falling behind because I’ll get stuck double-checking things that should be simple. Like, I’ll review a response before sending it, then review it again, then worry I misunderstood the issue, or that I didn’t document it clearly enough, or that I might have missed some obvious step. And then meanwhile the queue keeps building.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because coworkers have had to pick up some of the slack. No one has been cruel about it, but I can tell, and that makes me feel worse. I’ll see someone else take a ticket I should’ve handled, or they’ll gently ask if I’m okay, and then I start worrying about that too — like whether they think I’m unreliable.

And outside work, it’s affected things I actually care about. I’ve skipped several dance nights because getting myself there just feels like too much when I’m already overwhelmed. And I’ve missed mentoring sessions too, which I feel really guilty about, because that’s something I usually value and want to show up for. It’s not that I don’t care; it’s more like by the time it comes around, I feel so wound up and overloaded that I just can’t make myself go.
Do you have trouble sleeping because your mind keeps racing or you’re unable to relax, even when you’re tired?

Yes, definitely. That’s been happening most nights, honestly. I’ll be tired — like, really tired — and I’ll get into bed thinking I should fall asleep quickly because my body feels worn out, but then as soon as it’s quiet my brain just starts going.

It’ll replay work tickets, like whether I handled something correctly or missed a step, or whether I documented something clearly enough. Then it jumps to loan notices or bills or something I saw in the mail, and I start thinking, did I forget a deadline, did I misunderstand something, what if there’s a problem I didn’t catch. And then somehow I’m mentally going through all these little details that I can’t do anything about at that moment anyway.

I’ll try to tell myself, “You’re in bed, you can deal with it tomorrow,” but it doesn’t really settle. I keep feeling like I need to solve it before I can relax, except there’s nothing I can actually solve at 1 or 2 in the morning. A lot of nights I look at the clock and it’s suddenly 2 or 3 a.m., and then I get stressed about how little sleep I’m going to get, which makes it even harder.

And even when I do finally sleep, it doesn’t feel very restful. I wake up feeling like I barely slept, like my mind was still half-running the whole time.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of the times when you’re feeling anxious or wound up?

I’m not sure, honestly. I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless in a clear way, like I’ve given up on everything or anything like that. It’s more hard for me to separate what’s “feeling down” from just being exhausted and overwhelmed all the time.

Like, with things I usually enjoy, sometimes I don’t go or I don’t feel up for them, but I think that’s more because I’m tense or drained rather than because I don’t care about them anymore. If I actually imagine doing them on a day where I felt calmer, I think I would still want to. So I don’t know that it’s a loss of interest exactly.

I do get discouraged with myself, especially when I feel like I’m not keeping up or I’m disappointing people, but it feels tied to being wound up and stressed rather than this separate low mood that’s there on its own. I haven’t really noticed a separate “down” feeling outside of that, at least not in a way I could clearly point to.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of things, even small ones, not just major life events or problems?

Yes. It’s not just one big thing anymore, which is part of why it feels so exhausting. At first I could kind of tell myself, okay, I’m worried about the condo situation, that’s stressful, that makes sense. But now it’s like my mind doesn’t stay there — it jumps around to anything it can grab onto.

I’ll worry that my cousin is upset with me because of something small, like if a text sounded a little short or if I didn’t respond the “right” way. Then five minutes later I’m worrying about work, like whether I’m going to make some mistake on a support call or misunderstand what someone is asking for. And then it’ll shift again to money, like how I’m supposed to save enough or move forward in life if I’m already feeling behind.

It can be really small things too, not just major problems. I’ll take something ordinary and then my brain turns it into this whole chain of “what ifs.” It feels like I’m constantly scanning for what might go wrong next, even when there isn’t one clear emergency in front of me.

Have you ever experienced sudden, intense episodes of fear where you felt like something terrible was happening, such as your heart racing, feeling dizzy, or short of breath, even when there was no real danger?

I don’t think so… not in that really sudden, out-of-nowhere way you’re describing. I mean, I definitely get anxious and worked up, and sometimes it can feel intense, but it’s usually more like it builds because I’m thinking about something or worrying through a situation.

I don’t really remember having an episode where, all of a sudden, I felt like I was in immediate danger for no clear reason, like “something terrible is happening right now.” I might feel tense or uneasy, but I don’t think I’ve had that kind of abrupt wave of fear with the heart racing or dizziness or not being able to breathe in the way people describe.

I guess if anything, my fear tends to be more drawn out and tied to my thoughts, not like a sudden attack that peaks quickly. At least, not that I’ve noticed.
Would you say that your anxiety and worry happen on more days than not, and that it’s hard for you to control it, even when you try?

Yes, I’d say it’s more days than not. I don’t know if I notice it every single minute, but once it starts, it’s really hard to shut off. I’ll try to be logical with myself, like, “You already checked the spreadsheet,” or, “You already sent the email, there’s nothing else to do right now,” and for maybe a second that helps.

But then the thought just loops back around. Like, what if I missed something in the spreadsheet, or what if the email sounded wrong, or what if I sent it to the wrong person, or what if someone reads it and thinks I’m incompetent. It’s like one “what if” branches into five more before I can even catch up with it.

And I do try to stop it. I’ll reread things, or mentally review what I did, or tell myself I’m being unreasonable, but it doesn’t really feel under control. It’s more like I’m trying to pull myself back over and over again, and sometimes I can for a little while, but then my mind grabs onto the same thing or finds a new thing to worry about. So yes, it does feel pretty hard to control.

doctor.question: Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of the times when you’re feeling anxious or wound up?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about depressive symptoms such as low mood, hopelessness, or loss of interest, which are not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure, honestly. I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless in a clear way, like I’ve given up on everything or anything like that. It’s more hard for me to separate what’s “feeling down” from just being exhausted and overwhelmed all the time.

Like, with things I usually enjoy, sometimes I don’t go or I don’t feel up for them, but I think that’s more because I’m tense or drained rather than because I don’t care about them anymore. If I actually imagine doing them on a day where I felt calmer, I think I would still want to. So I don’t know that it’s a loss of interest exactly.

I do get discouraged with myself, especially when I feel like I’m not keeping up or I’m disappointing people, but it feels tied to being wound up and stressed rather than this separate low mood that’s there on its own. I haven’t really noticed a separate “down” feeling outside of that, at least not in a way I could clearly point to.

inference.note: This turn ruled out F32.0 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode) because the patient denied feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in activities outside of anxiety and stress. The remaining candidates are Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1) and Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety (F43.11), which remain plausible based on the presentation.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences excessive anxiety and worry about a number of events or activities, which is a key feature of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1), as opposed to Persistent Complex Bereavement Disorder (F43.11), which is tied more specifically to loss and would not typically present with generalized, persistent worry across multiple domains.
doctor.question: Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a variety of things, even small ones, not just major life events or problems?

target_item.name: Excessive_Anxiety_Worry
target_item.manifestation: My worry doesn't stay on the condo anymore; it jumps from whether my cousin is upset with me, to whether I'll make a mistake on a support call, to how I'll ever save money or move forward with my life.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the worry is excessive and spread across many different areas, including small things, rather than limited to one major problem.

patient.answer:
Yes. It’s not just one big thing anymore, which is part of why it feels so exhausting. At first I could kind of tell myself, okay, I’m worried about the condo situation, that’s stressful, that makes sense. But now it’s like my mind doesn’t stay there — it jumps around to anything it can grab onto.

I’ll worry that my cousin is upset with me because of something small, like if a text sounded a little short or if I didn’t respond the “right” way. Then five minutes later I’m worrying about work, like whether I’m going to make some mistake on a support call or misunderstand what someone is asking for. And then it’ll shift again to money, like how I’m supposed to save enough or move forward in life if I’m already feeling behind.

It can be really small things too, not just major problems. I’ll take something ordinary and then my brain turns it into this whole chain of “what ifs.” It feels like I’m constantly scanning for what might go wrong next, even when there isn’t one clear emergency in front of me.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences symptoms of panic attacks, which would support a diagnosis of panic disorder (F41.1) over generalized anxiety disorder (F43.11).
doctor.question: Have you ever experienced sudden, intense episodes of fear where you felt like something terrible was happening, such as your heart racing, feeling dizzy, or short of breath, even when there was no real danger?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about sudden intense panic-like episodes with physical symptoms such as racing heart, dizziness, or shortness of breath, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not in that really sudden, out-of-nowhere way you’re describing. I mean, I definitely get anxious and worked up, and sometimes it can feel intense, but it’s usually more like it builds because I’m thinking about something or worrying through a situation.

I don’t really remember having an episode where, all of a sudden, I felt like I was in immediate danger for no clear reason, like “something terrible is happening right now.” I might feel tense or uneasy, but I don’t think I’ve had that kind of abrupt wave of fear with the heart racing or dizziness or not being able to breathe in the way people describe.

I guess if anything, my fear tends to be more drawn out and tied to my thoughts, not like a sudden attack that peaks quickly. At least, not that I’ve noticed.

inference.note: The patient continues to endorse persistent, excessive worry across multiple domains, difficulty controlling anxiety, physical symptoms (muscle tension, restlessness, fatigue), impairment in daily functioning, and sleep disturbance, consistent with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1). No clear evidence of panic attacks or sudden surges of intense fear, which makes Panic Disorder (F41.0) less likely. There is no evidence of a traumatic stressor or persistent re-experiencing, which makes PTSD (F43.11) less likely, though it remains in the differential due to overlapping symptoms and the possibility of a trauma history not yet disclosed. No features of depression, OCD, or other primary disorders have emerged.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences excessive anxiety and worry that is difficult to control and occurs more days than not, which would support Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1).
doctor.question: Would you say that your anxiety and worry happen on more days than not, and that it’s hard for you to control it, even when you try?

target_item.name: Uncontrollable_Worry
target_item.manifestation: Even when I tell myself I've already checked the spreadsheet or sent the email, the thoughts keep looping, and one 'what if' turns into five more before I can pull myself back.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question most directly asks whether the anxiety and worry are hard to control, even when trying.

patient.answer:
Yes, I’d say it’s more days than not. I don’t know if I notice it every single minute, but once it starts, it’s really hard to shut off. I’ll try to be logical with myself, like, “You already checked the spreadsheet,” or, “You already sent the email, there’s nothing else to do right now,” and for maybe a second that helps.

But then the thought just loops back around. Like, what if I missed something in the spreadsheet, or what if the email sounded wrong, or what if I sent it to the wrong person, or what if someone reads it and thinks I’m incompetent. It’s like one “what if” branches into five more before I can even catch up with it.

And I do try to stop it. I’ll reread things, or mentally review what I did, or tell myself I’m being unreasonable, but it doesn’t really feel under control. It’s more like I’m trying to pull myself back over and over again, and sometimes I can for a little while, but then my mind grabs onto the same thing or finds a new thing to worry about. So yes, it does feel pretty hard to control.
